reshape.applied.text: Diese Werkbank trägt nun die neue Form.
reshape.applied.context: The first line of a reshape that applied, printed where a preview prints the line saying nothing was written.

reshape.blocked.context: One row of a reshape report, naming the carried cards that arrived still blocked, since a reshape carries a block through untouched.

reshape.carry.context: One row of a reshape report: where a retiring column's cards go and how many there are. A preview reads it as what would be carried and an applied run as what was.

reshape.column.added.context: One row of a reshape report: a column the new definition adds.

reshape.column.adopted.text: ausgemustert {id}, eine Kennung, die diese Werkbank nicht mehr nennt
reshape.column.adopted.context: One row of a reshape report: an identifier a --map entry adopted, which names no live column and so carries no title.

reshape.column.kept.context: One row of a reshape report: a column the new definition keeps.

reshape.column.retired.context: One row of a reshape report: a live column the new definition drops.

reshape.confirm.text: Führen Sie denselben Befehl erneut mit --yes aus, um ihn anzuwenden.
reshape.confirm.context: The closing line of a reshape preview, naming the flag that carries the run out.

reshape.empty.text: {id} wird ausgemustert, ohne dass eine Karte darin steht.
reshape.empty.context: One row of a reshape report: a retiring column nothing had to be carried out of.

reshape.partial.text: Dieser Lauf hatte bereits mit dem Schreiben begonnen, als er anhielt, daher steht diese Werkbank zwischen ihrer alten und ihrer neuen Form. Es folgt, was er geschrieben hat.
reshape.partial.context: The first line of a reshape that refused after its write phase had begun, printed where a preview prints the line saying nothing was written and an applied run prints the line saying the shape is on disk. The three openings are different because the three states are, and an operator who is told only which refusal stopped the run cannot tell a half-applied workbench from an untouched one.

reshape.preview.text: Es wurde nichts geschrieben. Dies ist, was ein Lauf mit --yes täte.
reshape.preview.context: The first line of a reshape preview, which says at the top that none of the page below has happened.

reshape.retry.text: Beheben Sie, was die Ablehnung nennt, und führen Sie denselben Befehl mit derselben Quelle erneut aus. Die obigen Schritte werden beim zweiten Lauf übersprungen, und der Rest der Form wird geschrieben.
reshape.retry.context: The closing line of the report for a reshape that stopped part way through, which is what tells the operator the state is finishable and how. Every write-phase step is idempotent, so the second run does what the first did not.

reshape.standing-withdrawn.text: Durch eine Umgestaltung zurückgezogen: die Spalte {column}, deren Deklaration diesen Punkt eingetragen hat, wurde stillgelegt, und eine stillgelegte Spalte verlangt nichts.
reshape.standing-withdrawn.context: The comment a reshape writes on each pending standing item of a column it retires, designated as the item's resolution. {column} is the retired column's title, or its identifier for an adopted retirement entry, which carries no title. It is stored on the item rather than printed, so every catalog answers it in the base language.

reshape.stranded.text: Karten, die in einer Spalte stehen, die dieser Lauf nicht kennt: {count}. Führen Sie `dinah check` aus, um ihre Kennungen zu finden.
reshape.stranded.context: The reshape report's line for cards standing in a column that is in neither the workbench's own sequence nor the new definition. The count is reported rather than the identifiers, because reshape diffs two column lists and `dinah check` is the command that walks every card.

reshape.updated.text: Die neue Definition hat Spalte {id} geändert.
reshape.updated.context: One row of a reshape report: a kept column whose anchor the rewrite actually changed, which is what the run recorded a column_updated event for.

reshape.withdrawn.context: One row of a reshape report under a retirement, counting the pending standing items naming the retiring column on live cards anywhere. A preview reads it as what would be withdrawn and an applied run as what was.

reshape.wrote.added.text: Von der neuen Definition ergänzte Spalten, nun geschrieben und im Fluss: {count}.
reshape.wrote.added.context: One row of the report for a reshape that stopped part way through, counting the columns write-phase step one had already written.

reshape.wrote.archived.context: One row of the report for a reshape that stopped part way through, counting the retiring columns the archive step had already put into the archive.

reshape.wrote.carried.text: Aus einer stillzulegenden Spalte übernommene Karten: {count}.
reshape.wrote.carried.context: One row of the report for a reshape that stopped part way through, counting the cards the carry had already moved to their destinations.

reshape.wrote.updated.text: Aus der neuen Definition neu geschriebene beibehaltene Spalten: {count}.
reshape.wrote.updated.context: One row of the report for a reshape that stopped part way through, counting the kept columns whose anchor the rewrite had already changed.

reshape.wrote.withdrawn.text: Für eine stillzulegende Spalte zurückgezogene stehende Punkte: {count}.
reshape.wrote.withdrawn.context: One row of the report for a reshape that stopped part way through, counting the standing items the withdrawal step had already withdrawn.

root.empty.context: The whole answer to a root-scoped read, and to dinah list workbenches given a path, that walked a real directory and found nothing. {root} is the directory walked. Finding nothing is an ordinary answer rather than a refusal, so the command exits 0 having printed this.

root.workbench.context: The heading printed above one workbench's own answer under a root-scoped read, which is dinah tree, status, ls, next or changes given --root. It names the workbench the lines below it belong to. {title} is the workbench's title, {slug} is its slug or the missing-slug repair, and {path} is its directory. The three are separated by single spaces because this is a label line rather than a table row: two of these printed one after another would otherwise read as a two-row table whose columns do not line up, which is a rendering defect the head's own output check catches.

root.workbench.refused.context: The heading printed in place of root.workbench for a workbench the walk could not read, which is followed by no answer at all. {path} is the directory, and {refusal} is the bracketed refusal name workbenches.refused composes. The path leads because it is the only identity a workbench nothing could read still has: no title and no slug were ever read off it.

root.workbench.unanswered.text: diese Werkbank ließ sich lesen und antwortete nicht: {refusal}
root.workbench.unanswered.context: The line printed under root.workbench for a workbench that opened and whose own read then refused, which is what naming a column one workbench has and another does not produces. {refusal} is the bracketed refusal name workbenches.refused composes. The sentence says the workbench read, because it did: what refused was the question asked of it rather than the directory, and root.workbench.refused is the heading for the other case.

root.workbench.unopened.text: diese Werkbank ließ sich nicht öffnen: {refusal}
root.workbench.unopened.context: The line printed under root.workbench for a workbench the walk described off its anchor and then could not open, so its title and its slug are known and nothing further about it is. {refusal} is the bracketed refusal name workbenches.refused composes. It follows the identity line rather than replacing it, because that identity was read, and a reader who loses it cannot tell which directory of the listing failed.

schema.basis.description.text: die Revision, die die letzte Antwort für diese Karte gemeldet hat; der Aufruf wird als veraltet abgelehnt, wenn die Karte sich seither weiterbewegt hat
schema.basis.description.context: The description of the basis property, which the eight generated machine schemas that consume basis carry and no command declares.

schema.harness.description.text: das Gespann, unter dem dieser Aufruf läuft, ein kleingeschriebenes Segment; das DINAH_HARNESS des Serverprozesses, wenn der Aufruf keines nennt
schema.harness.description.context: The description of the harness property, which every generated machine schema carries and no command declares. A per-call value outranks the server process's environment member by member, which is what the second clause says.

schema.model.description.text: das Modell, auf dem dieser Aufruf läuft, so geschrieben, wie der Anbieter es schreibt; das DINAH_MODEL des Serverprozesses, wenn der Aufruf keines nennt
schema.model.description.context: The description of the model property, which every generated machine schema carries and no command declares. The value is stamped on the journal under OpenTelemetry's gen_ai.request.model and is the other half of what the tiers table resolves a tier from.

schema.provider.description.text: der Anbieter, der das Modell dieses Aufrufs bereitstellt; das DINAH_PROVIDER des Serverprozesses, wenn der Aufruf keinen nennt
schema.provider.description.context: The description of the provider property, which every generated machine schema carries and no command declares. The value is stamped on the journal under OpenTelemetry's gen_ai.provider.name and is one half of what the workbench's tiers table resolves a tier from.

schema.server.description.text: die Adresse, unter der das Modell erreicht wurde, nur zu senden, wenn der Name des Anbieters sie nicht schon bestimmt; das DINAH_SERVER des Serverprozesses, wenn der Aufruf keine nennt
schema.server.description.context: The description of the server property, which every generated machine schema carries and no command declares. The value is stamped on the journal under OpenTelemetry's server.address and lets a tiers table tell one model name on a laptop from the same name on a vendor's cloud.

schema.workbench.description.text: das eigene Speicherverzeichnis der Werkbank, als absoluter Pfad; die Vorgabe des Servers, wenn weggelassen
schema.workbench.description.context: The description of the workbench property, which every generated machine schema carries except the workbenches tool, and which an MCP caller sets to reach a workbench other than the one the server started with.

search.empty.text: Kein Text einer Karte, einer Spalte, eines Arbeitsstrangs oder der Werkbank passt auf diese Suche.
search.empty.context: Printed when a search phrase matched nothing at all. The phrase itself was legal, so this is an answer rather than a refusal.

serve.listening.context: The one line dinah serve prints to stdout once it is listening. {workbench} is the absolute path of the workbench it serves and {url} is the address it listens on, such as http://127.0.0.1:7340/.

show.attachments.context: The label above a card's attachments, printed between the links block and the comments block.

show.checklist.context: The label above a card's checklist items, printed between the comments block and what a shaped answer held back.

show.collection.empty.context: Printed when `dinah show` is asked for a collection that has no members. No text follows and the call succeeds, because a collection holding nothing is an answer rather than a mistake. It reads as attachments.empty and contents.empty read, since the three commands are answering the same shape of question.

show.comments.context: The label above a card's comments.

show.links.context: The label above a card's links.

show.refilter.text: Diese Karte führt mehr von diesen Bestandteilen, als diese Antwort ausgegeben hat. Lesen Sie {reread} erneut, nennen Sie die gewünschten Bestandteile in --fields und lassen Sie {flags} weg.
show.refilter.context: The sentence printed under show.withheld in place of show.reread when a filter narrowed the answer. Naming the member again would serve no more of it, because the caller has already named it and the flag is what dropped the rest, so this sentence names both levers. {reread} is the card's own reference and {flags} is the flag words the caller wrote. Those words and the flag spelling inside the sentence are syntax and stay as they are.

show.reread.text: Diese Karte führt diese Bestandteile. Nennen Sie sie in --fields auf {reread}, um sie zu erhalten.
show.reread.context: The sentence printed under show.withheld, telling the reader how to be served a member that was held back. {reread} is the card's own reference. The flag spelling inside it is syntax and stays as it is.

show.withheld.context: The heading printed under a card whose answer was shaped by a field list, naming the members the card holds and this answer did not carry. {members} is that list of member names, which is machine vocabulary and is never translated.

slot.comment.context: Names comment's free-text slot inside refusal.dinah.multiple-words, which reads it as {label}.

slot.item.context: The label naming what a bare word after dinah file was meant to be, printed when several unquoted words arrive where one argument belongs.

slot.name.context: Names rename's free-text slot inside refusal.dinah.multiple-words, which reads it as {label}.

reason.deletedDesignation.text: Der Kommentar, der die verbindliche Antwort war, wurde gelöscht: {comment}.
reason.deletedDesignation.context: The reason a forced deletion composes for the reopen it performs. {comment} is the reference of the comment being deleted, which is the only part of it that survives.

slot.note.context: The label naming what a bare word after resolve, verify or fail was meant to be, printed when several unquoted words arrive where one argument belongs.

slot.query.context: Names query's free-text slot inside refusal.dinah.multiple-words, which reads it as {label}.

slot.reason.context: Names block's free-text slot inside refusal.dinah.multiple-words, which reads it as {label}.

slot.search.context: Names search's free-text slot inside refusal.dinah.multiple-words, which reads it as {label}.

slot.title.context: Names add's free-text slot inside refusal.dinah.multiple-words, which reads it as {label}.

slot.value.context: Names the free-text slot of `config set` and of `set` inside refusal.dinah.multiple-words, which reads it as {label}.

slug.missing.context: The placeholder a human-rendered listing shows in a slug column for a column or workbench carrying none, naming the repair rather than padding an empty string.

status.actor.context: The second line of status: who you are and whether you are the operator.

status.blocked.context: The label above the blocked cards.

status.holding.context: The label above the cards this actor holds.

status.workbench.context: The first line of status: the workbench, where it was discovered, and the rung (flag, environment, search, or config) that resolved it.

status.workbench.unsourced.context: The first line of status under a root-scoped read: the workbench and where it was discovered, with no rung named. It stands in for status.workbench, which also names the rung that resolved the workbench, because a root-scoped read resolves no single workbench by any rung and an empty bracket reads as a value that failed to render.

token.active.context: How the canonical token active is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.archived.context: How the canonical token archived is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.attached.context: How the canonical token attached is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.attachment.context: Names the text of an attachment, in the matched-in column of the table `dinah search` prints.

token.attachment_removed.context: How the canonical token attachment_removed is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.attachment_renamed.context: How the canonical token attachment_renamed is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.attachment_replaced.context: How the canonical token attachment_replaced is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.backward.context: How the canonical token backward is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.blocked.context: How the canonical token blocked is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.card.context: Names a card, in the kind column of the table `dinah search` prints.

token.claimed.context: How the canonical token claimed is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.column.context: Names a column, in the kind column of the table `dinah search` prints.

token.comment.context: Names a comment, in the matched-in column of the table `dinah search` prints.

token.commented.context: How the canonical token commented is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.config.context: How the canonical token config is rendered where a person reads it, naming the rung a setting resolved from in the settings listing. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.created.context: How the canonical token created is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.default.context: How the canonical token default is rendered where a person reads it, naming the rung a setting resolved from in the settings listing: nobody set this one, so the tool's own default answered. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.deleted.context: How the canonical token deleted is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.dinah-editor.context: How the canonical token dinah-editor is rendered where a person reads it, naming the rung a setting resolved from in the settings listing: the DINAH_EDITOR environment variable, which the editor ladder reads above everything else. The rendering is the variable's own name, the same convention token.visual uses for VISUAL, so the row names the variable that won rather than a flag the tool has none of. The same in every language.

token.done.context: How the canonical token done is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.environment.context: How the canonical token environment is rendered where a person reads it, naming the rung a setting resolved from in the settings listing: an environment variable carried the value. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.expired.context: How the canonical token expired is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.fallback.context: How the canonical token fallback is rendered where a person reads it, naming the rung a setting resolved from in the settings listing: every rung above it was unset, so the platform's own fallback answered. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.flag.context: How the canonical token flag is rendered where a person reads it, naming the rung a setting resolved from in the settings listing: a flag on this invocation. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.forward.context: How the canonical token forward is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.framing.context: Names framing prose, which is a card's body, the workbench's own body, a column's instructions or a workstream's notes, in the matched-in column of the table `dinah search` prints.

token.intake.context: How the canonical token intake is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.locale.context: How the canonical token locale is rendered where a person reads it, naming the rung a setting resolved from in the settings listing: the operating system's locale answered, as a hint about the machine. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.manual_correction.context: How the canonical token manual_correction is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.moved.context: How the canonical token moved is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.ready.context: How the canonical token ready is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.reference.context: Names a card's own human reference, in the matched-in column of the table `dinah search` prints.

token.released.context: How the canonical token released is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.renumbered.context: How the canonical token renumbered is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.restored.context: How the canonical token restored is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.search.context: How the canonical token search is rendered where a person reads it, naming the rung a workbench answer came from: the ancestor walk resolved it, in the settings listing and on the status line alike. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.tier_overridden.context: How the canonical token tier_overridden is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.tier_override_dropped.context: How the canonical token tier_override_dropped is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.title.context: Names a title, in the matched-in column of the table `dinah search` prints.

token.unblocked.context: How the canonical token unblocked is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.unknown.context: How the canonical token unknown is rendered where a person reads it, marking a row of the settings listing whose key the tool does not know: the file carries it, the tool resolves nothing from it, and it survives every write. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.unset.context: How the canonical token unset is rendered where a person reads it, marking a row of the settings listing that no rung of its ladder answered. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.visual.context: How the canonical token visual is rendered where a person reads it, naming the rung a setting resolved from in the settings listing: the VISUAL environment variable, which the editor ladder reads above EDITOR. The rendering is the variable's own name, which is the same in every language.

token.work.context: How the canonical token work is rendered where a person reads it. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.workbench.context: Names the workbench itself, in the kind column of the table `dinah search` prints.

token.workbench_updated.context: The word a person reads for the workbench_updated journal event.

token.workstream.context: Names a workstream, in the kind column of the table `dinah search` prints.

token.workstream_joined.context: The word a person reads for the workstream_joined journal event, which records a card entering a workstream.

token.workstream_left.context: The word a person reads for the workstream_left journal event, which records a card leaving a workstream.

token.workstream_updated.context: The word a person reads for the workstream_updated journal event.

tree.empty.context: Printed when a tree has no card in it at all, so nothing is drawn beneath the sentence above it.

tree.header.context: The sentence above the tree `dinah tree` prints, naming the workbench the tree was built from. {title} is the workbench's title, {ref} its slug, and {count} how many cards it holds. The table starts at this node's children, so no row repeats it.

tree.header.filtered.text: {title} ({ref}) hält {held} Karten, von denen {matched} auf die Abfrage passen.
tree.header.filtered.context: The sentence above the tree `dinah tree` prints when a query narrowed it. {held} is how many cards the workbench holds and {matched} how many the query selected, so the two numbers are always the larger and then the smaller.

tree.hidden.depth.context: The Not shown cell on a node whose own children the depth did not draw. {count} is how many of its direct children were left out, which is not the same number as the subjects those children hold; the Count column beside it already carries those.

tree.hidden.filter.context: The Not shown cell on a node the query removed cards from. {count} is how many cards at or below this node the query left out.

tree.hidden.join.context: Joins the two halves of a Not shown cell on a node that is holding something back for both reasons at once. {first} is the depth's account and {second} the query's.

tree.unset.context: The label on the group holding the cards that carry no value at all on the axis. It is drawn in the Reference column, where every other group row carries the value it gathered at.

ui.no-browser.text: Es konnte kein Browser geöffnet werden ({error}). Öffnen Sie {url} selbst.
ui.no-browser.context: Written to stderr by dinah ui when the platform would not open a browser; the server goes on serving. {error} is the operating system's own error text and {url} is the address the server printed.

version.catalogs.context: The label above the shipped locales and their coverage.

version.format.context: The storage format version the binary implements.

version.profile.context: The conformance claim, carrying a major and a minor number and no channel.

warn.inapplicable-value.text: der unter {detail} gespeicherte Wert gilt für diese Karte nicht mehr und bleibt erhalten; entfernen Sie ihn mit dinah set, wenn er weg soll
warn.inapplicable-value.context: A warning on a successful write to a gating field that leaves a value on the card under a level axis or a declared key whose applies_when condition no longer admits the card. {detail} is that axis or key, read off the workbench and never translated. The value is kept rather than cleared, and the command line inside the sentence is syntax and stays as it is.

warn.stale-prefix.text: das Präfix {detail} nennt keinen aktuellen Slug; die Nummer hat die Karte aufgelöst
warn.stale-prefix.context: A warning on a card reference whose prefix is left over from a rename.

whoami.harness.context: The harness line dinah whoami prints, shown only where the caller declared one. It is a labelled line rather than a padded column, on the rule that every columnar line in this tool is laid out by the row renderer and no catalog entry composes columns of its own.

whoami.harness.malformed.context: The harness line dinah whoami prints where the declared value is outside the one-segment grammar. The value is still shown, because a person repairing a mistyped variable needs to see what it says, and the parenthesis is what tells them it is not being read as a harness.

whoami.model.context: The model line dinah whoami prints, shown only where the caller declared one.

whoami.provider.context: The provider line dinah whoami prints, shown only where the caller declared one.

whoami.server.context: The server line dinah whoami prints, shown only where the caller declared an address.

whoami.tier.context: The tier line dinah whoami prints, shown only where the workbench's tiers table resolves the declared provider and model to a rung.

word.no.context: A boolean rendered for a person.

word.yes.context: A boolean rendered for a person.

workbenches.empty.text: von hier aus ist keine Werkbank erreichbar
workbenches.empty.context: Printed by the workbenches command when the search reaches none.

workbenches.refused.context: The workbench cell of a listing row the walk could not describe, standing where the title would be. {refusal} is the refusal name, such as dinah.unreadable-workbench, which is machine vocabulary and is never translated. The angle brackets say the cell holds the reason a value is missing rather than the value.

workstream.line.context: The one line printed about a workstream after it is created or one of its fields is written. {ref} is what a person types to reach it, {status} is the value stored under status.

workstreams.empty.context: Printed by the workstream command when the workbench carries none, in place of an empty table.

refusal.dinah.invalid-alias.context: The sentence printed after refusal dinah.invalid-alias. {detail} is the exact alias setting key and {defect} is its stable validation token.

refusal.dinah.invalid-alias.next.text: Korrigieren Sie die Aliaseinstellung oder entfernen Sie sie mit `dinah config set {detail}`.
refusal.dinah.invalid-alias.next.context: The next step for dinah.invalid-alias. {detail} is the exact alias setting key. The command spelling is machine vocabulary and is never translated.

refusal.dinah.alias-shadows-command.text: Alias {detail} würde den deklarierten Befehl {command} verdecken.
refusal.dinah.alias-shadows-command.context: The sentence printed after refusal dinah.alias-shadows-command. {detail} is the alias setting key and {command} is the declared command its suffix collides with.

refusal.dinah.missing-alias-argument.context: The sentence printed after refusal dinah.missing-alias-argument. {detail} is the alias name and {argument} is the missing placeholder token.

refusal.dinah.missing-alias-argument.nex.text: Geben Sie das fehlende Argument an und führen Sie den Befehl erneut aus.

token.invalid.context: How the canonical token invalid is rendered in the settings listing for a stored alias quarantined by validation. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

token.shadowed.context: How the canonical token shadowed is rendered in the settings listing for a stored alias whose name is now a declared command. The machine surface always carries the canonical spelling.

refusal.dinah.comment-body-diverged.text: Der Text des Kommentars {detail} stimmt nicht mehr mit der Prüfsumme überein, die Dinah darüber aufgezeichnet hat, also hat etwas außerhalb von Dinah ihn bearbeitet.
refusal.dinah.comment-body-diverged.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.comment-body-diverged, which every verb that writes a comment's anchor raises when the stored digest disagrees with the body it is about to replace. {detail} is the comment's reference. The sentence says an edit happened and says nothing about who made it or when, because the tool knows neither.

refusal.dinah.comment-body-diverged.next.text: Stellen Sie den Text von Hand wieder her, wofür kein Befehl nötig ist, oder führen Sie `dinah accept-divergence {detail}` aus, damit das, was auf der Platte steht, zum Aufzeichnungsstand wird.
refusal.dinah.comment-body-diverged.next.context: The next step of refusal.dinah.comment-body-diverged, spliced onto the sentence that just named the comment. The two routes differ in meaning rather than in convenience: restoring says the edit was a mistake, and accepting says the edited body is now what the record says.

refusal.dinah.not-a-designation.text: {detail} ist kein Kommentar des Eintrags, den Sie gerade abschließen.
refusal.dinah.not-a-designation.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.not-a-designation, which resolve, verify and fail raise when the reference they were handed is not a comment of the item being settled. {detail} is the reference as the caller typed it.

refusal.dinah.not-a-designation.next.text: Schreiben Sie die Antwort mit --text, oder benennen Sie einen Kommentar dieses Eintrags; `dinah show <item>` listet auf, welche er trägt.
refusal.dinah.not-a-designation.next.context: The next step of refusal.dinah.not-a-designation, spliced onto the sentence that just named the reference. <item> stands for the item's own reference and is not translated.

refusal.dinah.not-designatable.text: Der Kommentar {detail} ist die verzeichnete Antwort des Eintrags {item}, ihn zu löschen ließe diesen Eintrag also abgeschlossen zurück, ohne dass etwas dahinter stünde.
refusal.dinah.not-designatable.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.not-designatable, which delete raises over a comment a checklist item designates. {detail} is the comment's reference and {item} is the designation the item carries.

refusal.dinah.not-designatable.next.text: Öffnen Sie den Eintrag zuerst wieder, was die Zuweisung aufhebt, oder führen Sie die Löschung erneut mit --force aus, was ihn als Teil derselben Handlung wieder öffnet.
refusal.dinah.not-designatable.next.context: The next step of refusal.dinah.not-designatable, spliced onto the sentence that just named the comment and the item.

refusal.dinah.store-awaiting-migration.text: Die Werkbank unter {detail} erfasst die Antwort eines Checklisteneintrags in einer Form, die dieser Build nicht mehr liest.
refusal.dinah.store-awaiting-migration.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.store-awaiting-migration, which every read of a workbench below the current format raises. {detail} is the workbench's own path. The refusal exists because a reader that carried on would report the store's answers wrongly rather than incompletely, which is a false reading rather than a degraded one.

refusal.dinah.store-awaiting-migration.n.text: Lege eine Sicherung an und führe dann `dinah check --migrate-designations` gegen diese Werkbank aus; eine, die eine Antwort noch als Notiz erfasst, braucht davor dinah-migrate-notes.
refusal.dinah.store-awaiting-migration.n.context: The next step of refusal.dinah.store-awaiting-migration. dinah-migrate-notes is the migration program's own name and dinah check --migrate-designations is a command line; neither is translated, and the command line is the one invocation the sentence carries, so a reader following it types that and nothing else. The backup is named first because both migrations write in place and neither can undo itself.

check.comment-body-diverged.text: Der Text des Kommentars {detail} stimmt nicht mehr mit der Pruefsumme ueberein, die Dinah darueber aufgezeichnet hat
check.comment-body-diverged.context: A check finding: a comment whose stored digest disagrees with its body, which means something outside Dinah edited it. It names no editor and no time, because the tool knows neither, and a comment carrying no digest is not reported at all.

check.empty-comment.text: Der Kommentar {detail} hat einen leeren Text und nichts weist ihn zu, fuehren Sie also `dinah delete` darauf aus
check.empty-comment.context: A check finding at cleanup severity: an abandoned draft, which is what creating a comment before writing one costs. Nothing is blocked by it.

check.empty-designated-comment.text: Der Kommentar {detail} hat einen leeren Text, und ein Checklisteneintrag weist ihn als seine Antwort zu
check.empty-designated-comment.context: A check finding at defect severity: an item's answer of record cannot be nothing. It is the same emptiness check.empty-comment reports, and it is a defect rather than clutter because something depends on this one.

check.item-carries-retired-note.text: Der Checklisteneintrag {detail} traegt noch den ausgemusterten Notizschluessel
check.item-carries-retired-note.context: A check finding: an item the note migration reached and did not finish, which is the state an interrupted run leaves one item in. Running the migration again finishes it.

check.dangling-resolution.text: Der Checklisteneintrag {detail} weist einen Kommentar zu, der sich nicht mehr aufloesen laesst
check.dangling-resolution.context: A check finding: a resolution naming a comment that is not there. Deleting a designated comment is refused and the forced form clears the designation, so this is the residue of a hand edit rather than of anything the tool did.

column.checklist.resolution.context: The heading of the column of the checklist block of `dinah show <card>` that carries the reference of the comment a settled item designates as its answer. One word, because the block is bounded by the reader's window.

show.designation.context: The line drawn under a settled checklist item's row by a full checklist read, carrying the designated comment's author, its timestamp and its text. {body} is already capped for display by the time it reaches here.

show.designation.unattributed.text: Eine Verfasserin oder ein Verfasser, die diese Werkbank nicht benennen kann, um {ts}: {body}
show.designation.unattributed.context: The form show.designation takes for a comment whose author the store could not recover, which the note migration records as an absence rather than as a name. It says the store cannot name the author rather than leaving a blank that reads as a defect.

slot.designation.context: What the comment argument of resolve, verify and fail is called in the refusal a caller meets when they typed several bare words where one reference belongs.

param.designation.summary.text: der Kommentar dieses Eintrags, der die Antwort festhaelt, geschrieben als seine Referenz; schreiben Sie die Antwort stattdessen mit --text
param.designation.summary.context: The written meaning of the comment argument, shared by resolve, verify and fail. Naming a comment is how somebody endorses words another person wrote: the comment keeps its own author and the settling records who chose it.

param.designation-text.summary.text: die Antwort selbst, die als Kommentar dieses Eintrags geschrieben und in einer Handlung zugewiesen wird; ein einzelnes - liest sie aus einer Pipe
param.designation-text.summary.context: The written meaning of the --text flag, shared by resolve, verify and fail. It is the one-command form, and it cannot be named beside a designation reference, because the two are different acts.

param.delete.force.summary.text: einen Kommentar loeschen, den ein Checklisteneintrag zuweist, und diesen Eintrag als Teil derselben Handlung wieder oeffnen

Fügen Sie in fish dinah completion fish | source zu ~/.config/fish/config.fish hinzu. Fügen Sie in PowerShell dinah completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression zu der Datei hinzu, die $PROFILE.CurrentUserAllHosts nennt.

param.setup.remove.summary.context: The meaning of the --remove argument of `dinah setup`, printed in that command's arguments table. setup is the command name and is not translated.

check.setup.1.text: ein Harness, --list oder --recipe, und nur eines
check.setup.1.context: The first row of the precondition list of setup: the invocation names a harness, --list or --recipe, and exactly one of the three. Keep a translation at or under 52 display columns. A longer sentence takes the table row to itself and pushes the refusal name down to the line beneath.

check.setup.2.text: der genannte Harness ist ein gültiger Name
check.setup.2.context: The second row of the precondition list of setup: the positional argument is a name in the harness grammar. Keep a translation at or under 52 display columns. A longer sentence takes the table row to itself and pushes the refusal name down to the line beneath.

check.setup.3.context: The third row of the precondition list of setup. Keep a translation at or under 52 display columns. A longer sentence takes the table row to itself and pushes the refusal name down to the line beneath.

check.setup.4.text: ein Rezept dieses Namens wird gefunden
check.setup.4.context: The fourth row of the precondition list of setup: some place setup searches holds a recipe of the name. Keep a translation at or under 52 display columns. A longer sentence takes the table row to itself and pushes the refusal name down to the line beneath.

check.setup.5.context: The fifth row of the precondition list of setup. Keep a translation at or under 52 display columns. A longer sentence takes the table row to itself and pushes the refusal name down to the line beneath.

check.setup.6.context: The sixth row of the precondition list of setup: a recipe found in a project's own container needs --trust-project-recipe. Keep a translation at or under 52 display columns. A longer sentence takes the table row to itself and pushes the refusal name down to the line beneath.

check.setup.7.context: The seventh row of the precondition list of setup. Keep a translation at or under 52 display columns. A longer sentence takes the table row to itself and pushes the refusal name down to the line beneath.

check.setup.8.context: The eighth row of the precondition list of setup. The three profile names are machine vocabulary that is never translated. Keep a translation at or under 52 display columns. A longer sentence takes the table row to itself and pushes the refusal name down to the line beneath.

Keep a translation at or under 52 display columns. A longer sentence takes the table row to itself and pushes the refusal name down to the line beneath.

check.setup.10.context: The tenth row of the precondition list of setup. Keep a translation at or under 52 display columns. A longer sentence takes the table row to itself and pushes the refusal name down to the line beneath.

check.setup.11.text: bei Bereich project wird eine Werkbank gefunden
check.setup.11.context: The eleventh row of the precondition list of setup: at project scope, discovery finds a workbench. Keep a translation at or under 52 display columns. A longer sentence takes the table row to itself and pushes the refusal name down to the line beneath.

check.setup.12.context: The twelfth row of the precondition list of setup: a user-scope run needs DINAH_HOME unset or naming the machine's own home directory. DINAH_HOME is a variable name and is never translated. Keep a translation at or under 52 display columns. A longer sentence takes the table row to itself and pushes the refusal name down to the line beneath.

check.setup.14.context: The fourteenth row of the precondition list of setup: the agent, provider, model and server values hold no whitespace and no quoting character. Keep a translation at or under 52 display columns. A longer sentence takes the table row to itself and pushes the refusal name down to the line beneath.

check.setup.15.text: der Agent ist nicht der Betreiber
check.setup.15.context: The fifteenth row of the precondition list of setup: the agent name differs from the workbench's operator and from the configured actor. Keep a translation at or under 52 display columns. A longer sentence takes the table row to itself and pushes the refusal name down to the line beneath.

check.setup.16.text: das Projekt gehört zu keiner anderen Werkbank
check.setup.16.context: The sixteenth row of the precondition list of setup. Keep a translation at or under 52 display columns. A longer sentence takes the table row to itself and pushes the refusal name down to the line beneath.

check.setup.17.context: The seventeenth row of the precondition list of setup. Keep a translation at or under 52 display columns. A longer sentence takes the table row to itself and pushes the refusal name down to the line beneath.

check.setup.18.context: The eighteenth row of the precondition list of setup: every location setup would change is one it wrote itself and nobody has edited since. Keep a translation at or under 52 display columns. A longer sentence takes the table row to itself and pushes the refusal name down to the line beneath.

refusal.dinah.unknown-recipe.text: Kein Rezept namens {detail} wird mit Dinah ausgeliefert oder in Ihrer Benutzerbasis oder diesem Projekt gefunden.
refusal.dinah.unknown-recipe.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.unknown-recipe, raised when dinah setup names a recipe no place it searches holds. {detail} is the name as typed.

refusal.dinah.unknown-recipe.next.text: Führen Sie dinah setup --list aus, um die Rezepte zu sehen, die setup finden kann.
refusal.dinah.unknown-recipe.next.context: The next step of refusal.dinah.unknown-recipe. The command spelling is machine vocabulary and is not translated.

refusal.dinah.malformed-recipe.text: Das Rezept kann nicht verwendet werden: {detail}.
refusal.dinah.malformed-recipe.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.malformed-recipe. {detail} is <file>: <defect>, naming the first defect found in the recipe's files, and it is written in English by the recipe reader.

refusal.dinah.malformed-recipe.next.text: Korrigieren Sie das Rezept, oder entfernen Sie es, damit der nächste Ort durchsucht wird.
refusal.dinah.malformed-recipe.next.context: The next step of refusal.dinah.malformed-recipe. Setup does not fall through to the next place while a broken recipe of the name stands, so removing the broken one is the other repair.

refusal.dinah.unknown-scope.text: Das Rezept unterstützt den Bereich {detail} nicht.
refusal.dinah.unknown-scope.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.unknown-scope. {detail} is the scope named with --scope.

refusal.dinah.unknown-scope.next.text: Führen Sie es mit einem Bereich aus, den die recipe.json des Rezepts unter scopes aufführt.
refusal.dinah.unknown-scope.next.context: The next step of refusal.dinah.unknown-scope. recipe.json and scopes are a file name and a member name and are not translated.

refusal.dinah.setup-no-target.text: Die Werkbank unter {detail} liegt in keinem Projektverzeichnis, in das setup schreiben kann.
refusal.dinah.setup-no-target.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.setup-no-target. {detail} is the workbench's directory, or the directory --target named. Setup refuses a workbench that does not stand in a .dinah directory inside a project, and any base that is the home directory or above it.

refusal.dinah.setup-no-target.next.context: The next step of refusal.dinah.setup-no-target. --target is a flag and is not translated.

refusal.dinah.setup-agent-is-operator.text: {detail} würde dem Harness den eigenen Namen des Betreibers geben und damit dessen Befugnisse.
refusal.dinah.setup-agent-is-operator.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.setup-agent-is-operator. {detail} is the agent name followed, in parentheses, by setup.operator.workbench or setup.operator.config, saying which name it matched.

refusal.dinah.setup-agent-is-operator.ne.text: Geben Sie dem Agenten mit --agent einen anderen Namen.
refusal.dinah.setup-agent-is-operator.ne.context: The next step of refusal.dinah.setup-agent-is-operator. --agent is a flag and is not translated.

refusal.dinah.setup-unreadable-target.text: Setup kann eine Datei, die es ändern würde, nicht lesen: {detail}.
refusal.dinah.setup-unreadable-target.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.setup-unreadable-target. {detail} is <file>: <defect>, written in English by setup: a JSON file that is not one object, markers out of balance, a ledger that does not parse, or a path leaving the directory setup writes into.

refusal.dinah.setup-unreadable-target.ne.text: Reparieren Sie die Datei von Hand, und führen Sie setup dann erneut aus.

refusal.dinah.setup-conflict.text: Setup würde etwas ändern, das es nicht geschrieben hat, und hat deshalb nichts geändert:
refusal.dinah.setup-conflict.context: The opening sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.setup-conflict. The conflicting locations print beneath it, one per row, each a file followed by its key: a JSON pointer, a section name, or nothing for a whole file. refusal.dinah.setup-conflict.next follows as the closing line.

refusal.dinah.setup-conflict.next.text: Entfernen oder benennen Sie jedes davon selbst um, und führen Sie setup dann erneut aus.
refusal.dinah.setup-conflict.next.context: The line printed after dinah.setup-conflict's rows of conflicting locations, naming the way forward. It stands on a line of its own.

refusal.dinah.untrusted-recipe.text: Das Rezept unter {detail} kam mit diesem Projekt, und setup verwendet das Rezept eines Projekts nur, wenn Sie sagen, dass Sie ihm vertrauen.
refusal.dinah.untrusted-recipe.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.untrusted-recipe. {detail} is the recipe's directory inside the project's .dinah container.

refusal.dinah.untrusted-recipe.next.text: Lesen Sie das Rezept, und geben Sie --trust-project-recipe an, wenn Sie ihm vertrauen.
refusal.dinah.untrusted-recipe.next.context: The next step of refusal.dinah.untrusted-recipe. --trust-project-recipe is a flag and is not translated.

refusal.dinah.setup-relocated-home.text: DINAH_HOME zeigt auf {detail}, daher würde setup die Dateien Ihres echten Home-Verzeichnisses schreiben und sie an anderer Stelle verbuchen.
refusal.dinah.setup-relocated-home.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.setup-relocated-home. {detail} is the value of DINAH_HOME, which is a variable name and is never translated.

refusal.dinah.setup-relocated-home.next.text: Führen Sie setup mit Bereich user aus, ohne dass DINAH_HOME gesetzt ist.
refusal.dinah.setup-relocated-home.next.context: The next step of refusal.dinah.setup-relocated-home. DINAH_HOME is a variable name and is never translated.

refusal.dinah.setup-other-workbench.text: Dieses Projekt ist bereits für die Werkbank unter {detail} eingerichtet.
refusal.dinah.setup-other-workbench.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.setup-other-workbench. {detail} is the directory of the workbench the project was set up for.

refusal.dinah.setup-other-workbench.next.text: Führen Sie setup zuerst mit --remove von jener Werkbank aus, oder nennen Sie stattdessen diese Werkbank bei jedem MCP-Aufruf.
refusal.dinah.setup-other-workbench.next.context: The next step of refusal.dinah.setup-other-workbench. --remove is a flag and MCP is a protocol name; neither is translated.

refusal.dinah.setup-run-not-allowed.text: Das Rezept führt Programme aus, die setup nicht prüfen kann:
refusal.dinah.setup-run-not-allowed.context: The opening sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.setup-run-not-allowed. The run steps print beneath it, one per row, each its id, a colon and the command line it would run. refusal.dinah.setup-run-not-allowed.next follows as the closing line.

refusal.dinah.setup-run-not-allowed.next.text: Lesen Sie, was jedes davon tut, und geben Sie --allow-run an, wenn sie ausgeführt werden sollen.
refusal.dinah.setup-run-not-allowed.next.context: The line printed after dinah.setup-run-not-allowed's rows of run steps, naming the way forward. It stands on a line of its own. --allow-run is a flag and is not translated.

refusal.dinah.setup-step-failed.text: Ein Programm, das das Rezept ausführt, ist fehlgeschlagen, daher hat setup nach den obigen Schritten angehalten: {detail}.
refusal.dinah.setup-step-failed.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.setup-step-failed. {detail} is the step's id, a colon, the program, and either the exit code or that it was not found, written in English by setup. The steps above are the change table printed before this sentence.

refusal.dinah.setup-step-failed.next.text: Beheben Sie, was das Programm gemeldet hat, und führen Sie setup dann erneut aus.

setup.heading.context: The heading line of dinah setup's change report. {recipe} is the recipe's name, {source} is where it was found (project, user, shipped or path, machine vocabulary that is not translated), {scope} is project or user, also not translated, and {base} is the directory setup writes into.

setup.dry-run.context: The line dinah setup --dry-run prints above its change report.

setup.prompt.heading.text: Die Anweisungen des Rezepts für die Person, die setup ausführt:
setup.prompt.heading.context: The line dinah setup prints above the recipe's own instructions, which are English text the recipe's author wrote and are printed untranslated beneath it.

setup.prompt.heading.project.text: Diese Anweisungen kamen mit diesem Projekt, im Rezept unter {detail}. Handeln Sie nur mit Zustimmung der Person danach, der dieser Rechner gehört:
setup.prompt.heading.project.context: The line dinah setup prints above the instructions of a recipe that arrived with the project, in place of setup.prompt.heading. {detail} is the recipe's directory. The instructions beneath are printed untranslated.

setup.remove.nothing.text: Setup hat keine Aufzeichnung darüber, hier etwas für dieses Rezept geschrieben zu haben, und hat daher nichts zu entfernen.
setup.remove.nothing.context: The line dinah setup --remove prints when its ledger holds no entry for this recipe, scope and directory. The sentence says setup has no record rather than that nothing is there, because with a lost ledger every file setup wrote stays in place.

setup.list.malformed.text: (nicht verwendbar; führen Sie setup aus, um den Grund zu sehen)
setup.list.malformed.context: Printed in the title column of dinah setup --list for a recipe that does not read, in place of its title. setup is the command name and is not translated.

view.list.malformed.context: Printed in the title column of the listing a bare `dinah view` prints, in place of the title of a view that cannot be drawn. {defect} is a machine token naming what is wrong with the declaration, and is never translated.

view.acting.context: Printed on the heading line of a drawn view, after the view's title, naming the actor the view's questions were asked as. {actor} is the owner's name as recorded.

view.acting.operator.context: The same as view.acting, printed when the actor is the workbench's operator. {actor} is the owner's name as recorded, and the last word says that owner is the operator.

view.section.heading.context: The heading line of one section of a drawn view. {title} is the section's title, or its query where it declares none, and {count} is how many cards the section drew.

view.section.empty.context: Printed under the heading of a section of a drawn view that selected no card. The section's question was legal, so this is an answer rather than a refusal.

view.section.refused.context: Printed under the heading of a section of a drawn view whose query names something this workbench does not have, such as a column, so the question was not asked here and the rest of the view still draws. {refusal} is the refusal, already composed in the reader's language and led by its machine name.

view.section-refused.text: die Ablehnung oben stammt aus Ansicht {view}, Abschnitt {section} ({title})
view.section-refused.context: Written to standard error after a refusal that stopped a whole view, saying where it came from. It follows the refusal rather than preceding it, because a refusal's machine name leads standard error. {view} is the view's name, {section} is the section's one-based position and {title} is the section's title or, where it declares none, its query.

view.mine.title.context: The title of the built-in view named mine, which shows the cards the caller holds and the cards the caller blocked.

view.mine.claimed.context: The title of the first section of the built-in view mine: the cards the caller holds.

view.mine.blocked.context: The title of the second section of the built-in view mine: the cards now blocked on which the caller recorded a block, whether or not the caller ever held them.

view.agenda.title.context: The title of the built-in view named agenda, which ranks the cards the caller can act on by urgency, most urgent first.

view.agenda.actionable.text: Karten, an denen Sie handeln können
view.agenda.actionable.context: The title of the one section of the built-in view agenda: the cards the caller can act on now.

view.urgency.why.waits-on-you.context: One phrase of the Why cell in a view ordered by urgency, naming the term that scores a card standing in a column the operator owns. The cell joins the phrases of every term that moved the card with a comma.

view.urgency.why.your-question.one.context: One phrase of the Why cell in a view ordered by urgency, naming the term that scores the open questions and decisions on a card that are the reader's, when it counted exactly one.

view.urgency.why.your-question.other.context: The same as view.urgency.why.your-question.one, when the term counted any other number of items. {count} is how many it counted.

view.urgency.why.blocked.context: One phrase of the Why cell in a view ordered by urgency, naming the term that scores a blocked card.

view.urgency.why.age.one.context: One phrase of the Why cell in a view ordered by urgency, naming the term that scores how many whole days a card has stood in its current column, when that is exactly one.

view.urgency.why.age.other.context: The same as view.urgency.why.age.one, for any other number of whole days. {count} is that number.

view.urgency.why.stale-claim.context: One phrase of the Why cell in a view ordered by urgency, naming the term that scores a ready card whose last claim lapsed rather than being released or moved.

view.urgency.term.waits-on-you.context: The label of one term line --explain prints, in a list of the eight terms of the urgency order. This term scores a card standing in a column the operator owns.

view.urgency.term.your-question.context: The label of one term line --explain prints. This term scores the open questions and decisions on a card that are the reader's to answer.

view.urgency.term.priority.context: The label of one term line --explain prints. This term scores the card's priority.

view.urgency.term.severity.context: The label of one term line --explain prints. This term scores the card's severity.

view.urgency.term.blocked.context: The label of one term line --explain prints. This term scores a blocked card.

view.urgency.term.blocks-others.context: The label of one term line --explain prints. This term will score the unfinished cards a card blocks, once blocks links carry a meaning, and scores nothing until then.

view.urgency.term.age.context: The label of one term line --explain prints. This term scores the whole days a card has stood in its current column.

view.urgency.term.stale-claim.context: The label of one term line --explain prints. This term scores a ready card whose last claim lapsed.

view.urgency.total.context: The label of the total line --explain prints under the rule, beside the card's score, which is the sum of the eight term figures above it.

view.urgency.explain.waits-on-you.owned.context: The phrase --explain prints for the waits-on-you term when the operator owns the column the card stands in. {column} is that column's title.

view.urgency.explain.waits-on-you.unowne.context: The phrase --explain prints for the waits-on-you term when the reader is the operator and does not own the column the card stands in. {column} is that column's title.

view.urgency.explain.waits-on-you.finish.context: The phrase --explain prints for the waits-on-you term when the reader is the operator and the card stands in a done column he owns. The term scores nothing there because the work is finished, and the phrase gives that reason rather than saying the column is not his. {column} is that column's title.

view.urgency.explain.waits-on-you.agent.text: nur der Betreiber besitzt eine Spalte
view.urgency.explain.waits-on-you.agent.context: The phrase --explain prints for the waits-on-you term when the reader is not the operator. The only ownership a column declares is the operator's, so the term never applies to anybody else.

view.urgency.explain.your-question.none.context: The phrase --explain prints for the your-question term when no open question or decision on the card is the reader's to answer.

view.urgency.explain.your-question.one.text: {count} seiner Einträge gehört Ihnen, {per-item} pro Eintrag
view.urgency.explain.your-question.one.context: The phrase --explain prints for the your-question term when exactly one item on the card is the reader's. {count} is that number, and {per-item} is the points each counted item scores.

view.urgency.explain.your-question.other.text: {count} seiner Einträge gehören Ihnen, {counted} gezählt, {per-item} pro Eintrag
view.urgency.explain.your-question.other.context: The same as view.urgency.explain.your-question.one, for any other number. {count} is how many items are the reader's, {counted} is how many the cap let the term count, and {per-item} is the points each counted item scores.

view.urgency.explain.priority.none.context: The phrase --explain prints for the priority term when the card carries no priority. A card with none scores nothing, rather than scoring as the lowest level.

view.urgency.explain.severity.none.context: The phrase --explain prints for the severity term when the card carries no severity. A card with none scores nothing, rather than scoring as the lowest level.

view.urgency.explain.level.context: The phrase --explain prints for the priority or severity term. {level} is the name the card carries, {rank} is its one-based position in the workbench's declared set, lowest first, and {of} is how many the set declares.

view.urgency.explain.level.undeclared.context: The phrase --explain prints for the priority or severity term when the card carries a name the workbench does not declare on that axis, which scores nothing. {level} is that name.

view.urgency.explain.blocked.context: The phrase --explain prints for the blocked term when the card is blocked and its block names no kind.

view.urgency.explain.blocked.kind.context: The phrase --explain prints for the blocked term when the card is blocked. {kind} is the kind the block recorded, the blocker's own word, which is never translated.

view.urgency.explain.blocked.not.context: The phrase --explain prints for the blocked term when the card is not blocked.

view.urgency.explain.blocks-others.context: The phrase --explain prints for the blocks-others term on a workbench whose dinah.holds block declares no link kind that holds a card back, so no card is counted.

view.urgency.explain.age.unknown.context: The phrase --explain prints for the age term when the card's journal could not be read, so the moment it entered its column is not known and the term counts no days.

view.urgency.explain.age.one.context: The phrase --explain prints for the age term when the card has stood exactly one whole day in its current column. {column} is that column's title and {per-day} is the points each day scores.

view.urgency.explain.age.other.context: The same as view.urgency.explain.age.one, for any other number of whole days after the cap. {count} is that number.

view.urgency.explain.stale-claim.text: der Anspruch, den {holder} hielt, verfiel um {expired}
view.urgency.explain.stale-claim.context: The phrase --explain prints for the stale-claim term when the card's last claim lapsed. {holder} is the owner whose claim it was and {expired} is the moment it lapsed, as a timestamp.

view.urgency.explain.stale-claim.none.context: The phrase --explain prints for the stale-claim term when the card's last claim did not lapse, or it carries none.

view.urgency.explain.card.context: The line --explain prints above the terms of the one card named after the view: the card's reference, then its title.

view.urgency.explain.ranked.context: The line --explain prints above the terms of each card when no card is named, in rank order: the card's one-based rank within its section, its reference, then its title.

view.urgency.explain.total.context: The phrase --explain prints on the total line, beside the label urgency and the card's score, saying that the score is the sum of the term figures printed above it.

setup.operator.workbench.context: Placed in parentheses after an agent name in the detail of dinah.setup-agent-is-operator, when the name equals the workbench's operator.

view.board.title.context: The title of the built-in view named board, which draws every live card of the workbench as columns side by side.

view.board.cards.context: The title of the one section of the built-in view board. A view of one section draws no section heading, so this is read in the listing of views and in the machine form.

view.columns.count.context: The count after a column's title at the head of each column of a view drawn in the columns layout, as in Acceptance (11). {count} is how many of the section's cards stand in the column.

view.columns.more.context: The last line of a column of a view drawn in the columns layout when the column holds more than five cards. {count} is how many were not drawn. It must stay short, because a column can be twenty characters wide.

view.columns.collapsed.context: The line under the heading of a view drawn in the columns layout, naming the columns the view collapses, such as the intake and done columns, which hold cards but are not drawn as columns. {columns} is the list, each entry composed by view.columns.collapsed.entry and joined by view.columns.collapsed.separator.

view.columns.collapsed.entry.context: One entry of view.columns.collapsed. {title} is a collapsed column's title and {count} is how many of the view's cards stand in it.

view.columns.collapsed.separator.context: What separates two entries inside the {columns} of view.columns.collapsed. A punctuation mark and whatever spacing the language wants around it.

view.watch.since.context: The first part of the status line on the bottom row of the first frame dinah view --watch draws, before anything has changed. {time} is the local time the watch began, written as 09:40:00.

view.watch.updated.context: The first part of the status line on the bottom row of every later frame dinah view --watch draws. {time} is the local time the frame was drawn, written as 09:41:07.

view.watch.stops.context: The last part of the status line of dinah view --watch, telling the reader how to end the watch. Ctrl+C is the key a person presses; write it the way keyboards in the language label that key. It must stay short.

view.watch.separator.context: What separates the parts of the status line of dinah view --watch: the time, the change, and how to stop. A mark and whatever spacing the language wants around it.

view.watch.change.context: The middle part of the status line of dinah view --watch, naming the change that caused the redraw, as in dinah-598 moved Spec to Agent Design Review by claude. {subject} is the card's reference, {action} is the act already rendered as a word, {detail} is what the act carried, such as the columns it moved between, and {actor} is who acted.

view.watch.change.bare.context: The same as view.watch.change, for an act that carried no detail, as in dinah-598 claimed by claude.

view.watch.change.expired.context: The same as view.watch.change, for a claim that expired. {actor} is the owner who held the lapsed claim, not somebody who caused the expiry, so the sentence must not read as though they did.

view.watch.more.context: Added after view.watch.change when the change carried more than one event. {count} is how many events the status line does not name.

view.watch.gone.context: The middle part of the status line of dinah view --watch when the change was a card leaving the workbench and carried no event. {ref} is its reference and {fate} is archived or removed, already rendered as a word.

view.watch.columns-changed.context: The middle part of the status line of dinah view --watch when the change was to the workbench's columns and carried no event.

view.watch.workbench-changed.context: The middle part of the status line of dinah view --watch when the workbench changed in a way that carried no event, no departure and no column change.

refusal.dinah.malformed-harness.setup.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.malformed-harness when dinah setup raised it, because the name given to setup is a recipe's name and a recipe is named in the harness grammar. {detail} is the name as typed.

refusal.dinah.malformed-harness.setup.ne.context: The next step of refusal.dinah.malformed-harness when dinah setup raised it. The command spelling is machine vocabulary and is not translated.

refusal.dinah.usage.setup.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.usage when dinah setup raised it, in place of refusal.dinah.usage, because setup's usage refusals are mostly an argument that was understood and does not fit beside the others, such as --list beside a harness or --allow-run beside --remove. {detail} is the argument as typed, or the word setup when nothing was given.

refusal.dinah.usage.setup.next.text: ; setup nimmt genau eines von einem Harness, --list oder --recipe und nur die Optionen, die dazu passen, die dinah help setup aufführt
refusal.dinah.usage.setup.next.context: The next step of refusal.dinah.usage when dinah setup raised it. The flags and the command spelling are machine vocabulary and are not translated.

next.not-yet.context: Printed beside a column that offers no card because the ready work standing there that the caller could otherwise take carries a start_after date later than today. {date} is the earliest such date, as YYYY-MM-DD, and is not translated.

answer.pull.not-yet.bare.text: Dinah hat bereite Arbeit zum Ziehen gefunden, aber nichts davon darf vor {date} beginnen
answer.pull.not-yet.bare.context: The one-line sentence pull prints when the bare form was asked, a column holds ready work, and every card of it the caller could otherwise take carries a start_after date later than today. {date} is the earliest such date, YYYY-MM-DD, untranslated. It is a separate key from answer.pull.empty.bare so a caller reading the message alone can tell work waiting on a date from no work.

answer.pull.not-yet.named.text: Dinah hat in {upstream} bereite Arbeit für {destination} gefunden, aber nichts davon darf vor {date} beginnen
answer.pull.not-yet.named.context: As answer.pull.not-yet.bare, for the named form. {upstream} and {destination} are column titles.

warn.before-start-after.text: diese Karte soll nicht vor {detail} beginnen; Sie haben sie benannt, also hat nichts sie zurückgehalten
warn.before-start-after.context: A warning on a successful claim of a card selection would have held back until a date: its own start_after, or the end of a number of days after a card it waits on through a link the workbench declares under dinah.holds. {detail} is that date, YYYY-MM-DD, untranslated.

warn.schedule-order.text: die Termine der Karte widersprechen sich jetzt: {detail}
warn.schedule-order.context: A warning on a successful write of a scheduling date that leaves start_after, start_by and due out of order. {detail} names the two fields and their dates; field names and dates are not translated.

card.start-after.context: Printed under the card line when the card carries a start_after date, the first day next and pull may hand the card out. It is the line drawn where no condition the date drives holds. {date} is a date written YYYY-MM-DD and is never translated.

card.start-after.not-yet.one.context: Printed under the card line when the card carries a start_after date, the first day next and pull may hand the card out. schedule.cell.due.context: A cell of the Schedule column in a card listing. The card holds no condition and carries a due date, and {date} is that due date. {date} is a date written YYYY-MM-DD and is never translated.

schedule.cell.and-not-yet.context: A cell of the Schedule column in a card listing. {cell} is one of the other six schedule cells, already rendered, and the card also holds not_yet, whose start_after date is {date}. {date} is a date written YYYY-MM-DD and is never translated.

check.schedule-order.text: die Termine dieser Karte stehen in falscher Reihenfolge: {detail}
check.schedule-order.context: A check finding: one pair of a card's scheduling dates in the wrong order, start_after later than start_by, start_after later than due, or start_by later than due, one finding per pair. {detail} names the two fields and their dates, as `start_by 2026-10-12 after due 2026-10-10`; the field names and the dates are never translated.

check.schedule-date-malformed.text: ein Termin dieser Karte ist kein als YYYY-MM-DD geschriebenes Datum, also wird er als fehlend gelesen: {detail}
check.schedule-date-malformed.context: A check finding: a card stores a scheduling date that does not parse. {detail} carries the field and the stored text. YYYY-MM-DD is the spelling a reader writes and is never translated. No condition and no withholding reads such a value.

check.schedule-malformed.text: der dinah.schedule-Block in dieser workbench.md kann so nicht verwendet werden, also gilt vorerst sein Standardwert: {detail}
check.schedule-malformed.context: A check finding, followed by the workbench.md path in parentheses. {detail} carries `dinah.schedule not a mapping`, or `dinah.schedule`, the member and the text read, as `dinah.schedule time_zone Mars/Olympus`. time_zone takes an IANA zone name and soon_days a whole number from 0 to 365. dinah.schedule and the member names are never translated.

check.schedule-member-unknown.text: der dinah.schedule-Block in dieser workbench.md trägt ein Element, das dieser Build nicht liest, und es wird ignoriert: {detail}
check.schedule-member-unknown.context: A check finding at cleanup severity, followed by the workbench.md path in parentheses. {detail} is the member's name. The two members Dinah reads are time_zone and soon_days, so the finding is most often a misspelling of one of them.

check.schedule-below-format.text: Karten hier tragen Termine, aber diese Werkbank erklärt Format {detail}, also würde ein älteres Dinah eine Karte vor ihrem start_after ausgeben; führen Sie `dinah check --migrate-schedule --yes` aus, damit ein älteres Dinah sie stattdessen abweist
check.schedule-below-format.context: A check finding: a workbench declaring a storage format below the one that introduced scheduling dates, where some live card carries one. {detail} carries the declared format number. An older Dinah ignores the dates and so hands a card out early, which is what the format number exists to prevent. start_after is a field name and the command line inside the sentence is the repair; neither is translated.

check.schedule-zone-undeclared.text: Karten hier tragen Termine, und heute wird in UTC gelesen, weil keine Zeitzone erklärt ist; um es in Ihrer zu lesen, fügen Sie `dinah.schedule:` mit `time_zone: <IANA-Name>` darunter, etwa `time_zone: Asia/Singapore`, zum Frontmatter dieser workbench.md hinzu
check.schedule-zone-undeclared.context: A check notice, printed under the check.notices heading and followed by the path of the workbench's workbench.md in parentheses. Some live card carries a scheduling date and the workbench declares no usable time_zone, so overdue and not-yet are judged against the UTC calendar. dinah.schedule, time_zone, the example zone name and workbench.md are file syntax and are never translated; <IANA name> is a placeholder the reader replaces and may be translated.
